column1: # Reviewed semantic comparators for the eleven declared-volatile tour rows.
# Sprint 118 / Story #4 / Story-ID 759341a95870.
# STATUS: THIS TABLE HAS GATE EFFECT. It is the manager-adjudicated resolution
# of the open item docs/tour/volatility.tsv raised: those rows cannot
# reproduce a byte-exact digest, and the sprint-118 plan §6 allows exactly two
# outs — a real environment control, or an explicit reviewed semantic
# comparator that verifies values, ranges, event multiplicity, causal order and
# timing conditions. This is the second. The upstream sources stay byte-for-byte
# unchanged (story 2daf permits checked-in adapters and narrow normalizers, not
# edits to the corpus), and tools/tour/normalize.rb keeps its minimal
# tour-normalizer/v1 rules: nothing is masked.
# WHAT A COMPARATOR REPLACES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
#   Replaced: byte-identity of the STDOUT ELEMENTS named in `volatile_element`.
#   Untouched: exit status and stderr, which are still compared EXACTLY, and
#   every other byte of stdout, which is still compared literally by the
#   comparator's own invariants.
# HOW THE COMPARISON IS ANCHORED. Not to the historical frozen draw. Each
# comparator is evaluated against an ORACLE: repeated observations of the
# native binary freshly built from that row's unchanged upstream source in the
# same run, bound in the ledger by the binary's digest (tools/tour/executor-runner.rb
# runs TOUR_ORACLE_REPEATS of them, default 7). Ranges and multiplicities come
# from those real repeats. Every invariant is applied to every oracle
# observation too, so a comparator that does not describe the real program
# fails on the oracle before it can excuse a candidate. The pinned accepted
# observation in tests/tour/results.tsv is retained for these rows as
# HISTORICAL evidence of one draw on one day and is no longer a required
# output; see docs/tour/executor.md, "Semantic migration".
# COLUMNS
#   path              inventory row the comparator is bound to
#   comparator        implementation in tools/tour/semantics.rb
#   source_sha256     the pinned source digest; the loader refuses to bind a
#                     comparator to a row whose inventory digest differs, so a
#                     comparator can never be retargeted at another program
#   burst_variation   `required` when the volatile element MUST differ across
#                     the oracle repeats (a PRNG draw, a nanosecond clock, a
#                     goroutine race). An oracle with one distinct stdout then
#                     fails: it is evidence the comparator is not needed here.
#                     `not_required` for elements that legitimately hold still
#                     inside one burst — the two date/hour branches (the clock
#                     does not cross a boundary in a few seconds), the
#                     two-entry map orders (a seven-run sample can draw one
#                     order with probability 2^-6) and the channel arrival
#                     order of concurrency/channels.go (measured flip rate
#                     about 1/400 under GOMAXPROCS=2, so a seven-run burst
#                     legitimately drew one single order 7/7).
#   volatile_element  the element the comparator adjudicates, verbatim from
#                     docs/tour/volatility.tsv
#   params            comparator parameters as JSON; pinned expectations taken
#                     from the upstream source itself
# NEGATIVE COVERAGE. tools/tour/semantics-selftests.rb drives every comparator
# with wrong values, wrong counts, wrong sets, wrong order, wrong exit status,
# wrong stderr and wrong timing, and requires each to be REJECTED; it also
# proves each comparator rejects the *other* rows' outputs.
